clips.text: Welcome aboard our Schweizer two thirty-three. I will fly while you enjoy the view. This is a simulated local discovery flight. Open Menu whenever you want to pause or finish.
Welcome aboard. This shorter tour starts already airborne. I have the controls. We will look for rising air, enjoy the Boulder panorama, and return for an unpowered landing.
The towplane is taking us up. Notice the rope ahead and the small control corrections. The sailplane has no engine; the tug supplies the energy for this climb.
We have reached our release area. Releasing now. Watch the towplane separate, and listen as its engine fades away.
We are looking for a column of rising air called a thermal. I will turn smoothly to stay with the lift. The sound and instruments will help us tell whether we are climbing.
Now we are gaining energy in the rising air. We can climb without an engine because the air is rising faster than the sailplane sinks through it.
We have gained some height. Let us use it for a look around Boulder. You can keep enjoying the view, or choose Take control from Menu during a stable glide.
We are returning to the airport with height in reserve. In a sailplane, we plan the landing before that margin gets small.
The lift or our remaining height calls for an earlier return. We will shorten the sightseeing and keep a useful landing margin.
The airport is ahead. I am arranging our unpowered landing circuit. Airbrakes will help control the descent while pitch controls our speed.
We are lined up for landing. Notice the airbrake handle moving as I adjust the approach. I will round out close to the surface and brake after touchdown.
We have landed and stopped. The sailplane cannot taxi under its own power. Open Menu to repeat the tour, choose a lesson, or finish the flight.
You have the controls. Make small, coordinated movements and keep a safe airspeed. The pause menu lets you ask me to resume, or return to the airport.
I have the controls. I will continue from our current position, keeping the airport within reach.
Boulder Reservoir is the broad stretch of water to the north. It is a recreation area and a water-storage facility, and a useful landmark for finding the airport.
Mount Sanitas marks part of the foothill edge west of Boulder. Notice how quickly the open plains rise into wooded slopes.
Those tilted rock formations are the Flatirons, with Green Mountain behind them. We are enjoying the panorama from this side of the foothills.
Downtown Boulder lies below the foothills. From here, you can see the city spread eastward onto the plains.
That is the University of Colorado Boulder campus, south of downtown. The campus and the mountain backdrop are familiar landmarks on a local scenic flight.
There is Boulder Municipal Airport. Keep it in view as we prepare to return. We share the area with other aircraft and gliders.
Look ahead on the left. A golden eagle is circling in the rising air. We will give it room and enjoy the view.
Look ahead on the right. A golden eagle is circling in the rising air. We will give it room and enjoy the view.
Look ahead and slightly above us. A golden eagle is using the rising air too. We will give it room.
